daily_brief: The day's most significant developments center on escalating regional conflicts and diplomatic tensions. Bulgaria summoned Russia's ambassador after drone attacks sank a merchant ship in the Black Sea, leaving 11 crew missing—the latest in a series of strikes that NATO allies are monitoring closely [BBC, Le Monde, Financial Times]. The EU expressed cautious skepticism toward President Trump's proposed 'energy ceasefire' between Russia and Ukraine, with Kyiv reporting continued Russian strikes on energy infrastructure despite the announced deal [RFI]. In a dramatic political realignment, former DRC President Joseph Kabila announced he would lead a new 'politico-military' alliance with the M23 rebel group controlling eastern Congo, marking a significant escalation in his confrontation with President Tshisekedi's government [RFI]. Maritime security concerns intensified as Iran launched its worst spate of attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz since the war began, targeting 24 vessels in two weeks [Financial Times], while the UK's MI5 chief warned of a 'major shift' in Iranian targeting of British military sites [Financial Times]. The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to ICJ Judge Navi Pillay, who chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel committed genocide in Gaza—a selection likely to draw sharp international reactions [The Guardian].

top_stories.headline: Bulgaria Summons Russian Ambassador After Drone Attack Sinks Ship, Leaves 11 Missing
bullets: Two merchant ships were struck by drones off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast; one sank 31km east of Krapets village with 11 crew missing and one rescued
Bulgarian PM Rumen Radev convened emergency meeting and summoned Russian ambassador, stating 'the logic suggests the outcome benefits the Russian Federation'
Russian ambassador Eleonora Mitrofanova denied having information from Moscow and suggested the strikes could be a 'third party provocation'
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte spoke with Radev, pledging continued close work with Black Sea allies; this follows last week's sinking of the Alfa Watan which left 10 crew presumed dead

sources.name: BBC
sources.framing_note: Detailed factual coverage emphasizing NATO coordination

sources.name: Le Monde
sources.framing_note: Article content unavailable but headline confirms coverage

sources.name: Financial Times
sources.framing_note: Brief coverage framing as 'latest escalation' in Russia-Ukraine war

top_stories.headline: EU Skeptical of Trump's 'Energy Ceasefire' as Russia Continues Ukraine Strikes
bullets: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Brussels wanted 'clear evidence' Moscow would respect the proposed halt to attacks on energy infrastructure
Ukraine's President Zelensky stated 'it is increasingly evident that Russia is unwilling to accept an energy ceasefire proposed by the United States'
Trump defended a temporary easing of US sanctions on Russian diesel despite criticism from US lawmakers in both parties
European allies expressed unease after the sanctions relief, fearing it could reduce pressure on Putin to end the war

sources.name: RFI
sources.framing_note: Emphasized European skepticism and Ukraine's position that Russia was not honoring the deal

top_stories.headline: Former DRC President Kabila Announces Alliance with M23 Rebels to Overthrow Tshisekedi
bullets: Joseph Kabila, who ruled DRC from 2001-2019, unveiled the 'Front pour la Refondation de la Nation' at a press conference at his residence in M23-controlled Goma
The alliance's stated objective is to 'put an end to tyranny by any means, including force,' with Kabila as leader and senior M23 figures as deputies
Kabila was sentenced to death in absentia in 2025 after being convicted of 'complicity' with the Rwanda-backed M23 movement
The announcement represents a significant escalation, uniting one of DRC's most prominent political figures with an armed group controlling large areas of eastern Congo

sources.name: RFI
sources.framing_note: Straightforward reporting on the alliance formation and its implications for Congo's stability

top_stories.headline: ICJ Judge Navi Pillay Awarded Nobel Peace Prize for International Law Work
bullets: The Norwegian Nobel Committee cited Pillay's demonstration that 'legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence'
Pillay chaired the UN commission that concluded last year Israel was guilty of 'genocidal acts in Gaza' with 'specific intent to destroy Palestinians'
The committee highlighted her career from defending Nelson Mandela under apartheid to serving as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
Israel had refused to cooperate with her commission, calling it biased, and rejected its genocide report as 'scandalous'

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Detailed coverage of Pillay's career and the genocide findings, noting Israel's rejection of the commission

top_stories.headline: Iran Launches Worst Spate of Attacks on Strait of Hormuz Shipping Since War Began
bullets: Twenty-four tankers and other vessels were targeted by Iran in the Strait of Hormuz over two weeks, including six on Sunday alone
UK's MI5 chief Ken McCallum warned Iran has made a 'major shift' to target British military sites
McCallum stated both Tehran and Moscow are seeking to escalate hybrid warfare, with state threats quadrupling in a decade
UK PM Burnham leveled 'sweeping accusations' at Iran and Russia over hostile activities

sources.name: Financial Times
sources.framing_note: Focused on scale of attacks and intelligence assessment of Iranian strategic shift

sources.name: Le Monde
sources.framing_note: Headline confirms UK PM accusations against Iran and Russia
